title: PSOEXpert -molecular Classifier PsorX-LabDisc (CE-IVD) to distinguish psoriasis from eczema
summary:
Skin conditions like psoriasis and eczema can sometimes look very similar, especially when they affect the hands, feet, or scalp. However, telling them apart is becoming increasingly important because new and improved treatments only work if the diagnosis is correct.

To help with this, a new test called PsorX-LabDisk has been developed. It analyzes skin samples at the genetic level using RT-PCR technology and can accurately distinguish between psoriasis and eczema—even in cases where traditional diagnostic methods fail. The test works with preserved skin samples that are already collected as part of routine medical procedures.

To better understand how useful PsorX-LabDisk is in everyday clinical practice, a study called PSORXpert will be conducted. It will examine skin samples from 150 patients (75 with psoriasis and 75 with eczema) that were previously collected. The test results will be compared with the patients’ original diagnoses to measure how accurately PsorX-LabDisk identifies each condition. The goal is to determine how sensitive and specific the test is in distinguishing between the two diseases.

interventions.name:
Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) skin samples, previously collected as part of routine diagnostics from patients diagnosed with psoriasis and eczema, will be used to perform the PsorX assay once:
a) manually, and
b) using the PsorX-LabDisk (CE-IVD) cartridge.
